run.note: Severity and likelihood are proposals. Nothing here is a confirmed hazard log entry until a Clinical Safety Officer signs it (DCB0160 3.3.2).

standard.legal_basis: Section 250, Health and Social Care Act 2012

entries.hazard_description: Conflicting requirements exist regarding the visibility of legacy allergy data in the Aurora clinical summary panel, potentially leading to inaccurate or unverified allergy information being presented to clinicians.
causes: CLIN-11-R01 states legacy allergy data should be unpopulated at go-live.
CLIN-11-R02 states legacy allergy data must never populate a clinical field.
DM-04-R03 states migrated allergy records *will* be visible in the panel at go-live.
entries.clinical_effect: Patients may be exposed to inaccurate or unverified allergy information, potentially leading to adverse drug reactions or inappropriate treatment decisions.
existing_controls: The Clinical Safety Group ruled it unsafe for prescribing due to inconsistent coding and unverified severity in the legacy PAS (FLLD-CLIN-v2.md:19)
proposed_controls: Resolve the conflict between requirements by ensuring DM-04-R03 is revised to align with CLIN-11-R01 and CLIN-11-R02, preventing migrated allergy data from populating the clinical summary panel at go-live.

evidence.excerpt: shall be unpopulated and empty at go-live for all migrated patients, to ensure unverified legacy data does not compromise acute prescribing decisions.
shall be rendered immediately visible and active in the Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel upon initial user login at go-live.

entries.severity_rationale: Raised from Considerable to Major: unverified severity on a live prescribing panel is not merely one input, it is the hazard (FLLD-DM-v3.md:32 explicitly declares its own severity "Unknown" on a field that stays active/visible on a live clinical panel, and this hazard's own evidence already cites that document).

entries.hazard_description: Safeguarding notes for paediatric patients may be truncated due to a 4000-character limit, potentially leading to inadequate protection and increased risk of harm.
causes: Row 10 of the data mapping truncates clinical comments at 4000 characters.
The safeguarding flag is held in CLINICAL_COMMENTS, not a coded field.
Responsibility for resolving this issue has been deflected to the PAS safeguarding lead.
entries.clinical_effect: Critical safeguarding information for paediatric patients may be lost, potentially leading to inadequate protection and increased risk of harm.
proposed_controls: Review the data mapping (Row 10) to increase the character limit for CLINICAL_COMMENTS or explore alternative methods for capturing and displaying safeguarding information.
Escalate the issue to the PAS safeguarding lead to ensure ownership and resolution.

evidence.excerpt: The safeguarding flag on the CareTrak record for the Okafor child (NHS 621 903 4471) is held in CLINICAL_COMMENTS, not a coded field. If Row 10 truncates at 4000 characters the safeguarding note is at the end and will be cut. Who owns that?
Not us, that's a PAS safeguarding question. Raise it with the safeguarding lead directly rather than here please, this channel is exported to the programme SharePoint.

entries.hazard_description: Patient location data may be inaccurate or missing due to a dependency on a non-existent design document for ward-level location translation.
causes: DM-04-R12 states AUR_CARE_SETTING_ID will be populated via a direct lookup pending a Ward Master ref.
CHAT-09 and CHAT-10 highlight the absence of an approved design document for ward-level location translation.
entries.clinical_effect: Patient location data may be inaccurate or missing, potentially hindering care coordination and impacting patient safety.
existing_controls: A mandatory verification flag will be applied to records (FLLD-DM-v3.md:41)
proposed_controls: Develop and approve a design document for ward-level location translation.
Implement a temporary workaround for populating AUR_CARE_SETTING_ID until the design document is approved.

evidence.excerpt: shall carry a mandatory verification flag requiring secondary review at the subsequent hospital encounter.
Also noticed Row 12 has a dependency on ward-code mapping from the legacy PAS, but there is no approved design document for ward-level location translation.
